4:1.sourceText: Μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ θύρα ἠνεῳγμένη ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἡ φωνὴ ἡ πρώτη ἣν ἤκουσα ὡς σάλπιγγος λαλούσης μετ’ ἐμοῦ, λέγων Ἀνάβα ὧδε, καὶ δείξω σοι ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι μετὰ ταῦτα.
4:1.targetText: After this I looked and saw a door standing open in heaven. And the voice I had previously heard speak to me like a trumpet was saying, “Come up here, and I will show you what must happen after these things.”

groups.note: The plural ταῦτα ("these things") is rendered this.
ἰδού ("behold"), which brings in what John sees, is rendered saw.
The adjective πρώτη ("first") marks the voice John heard first (1:10); BSB renders it previously.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The repeated article of the adjective πρώτη has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the relative ἥν ("which") without an English word.

4:2.sourceText: εὐθέως ἐγενόμην ἐν Πνεύματι· καὶ ἰδοὺ θρόνος ἔκειτο ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν θρόνον καθήμενος,
4:2.targetText: At once I was in the Spirit, and I saw a throne standing in heaven, with someone seated on it.

groups.note: ἰδού ("behold"), which brings in what John sees, is rendered I saw.
ἔκειτο ("was set, stood") is rendered standing.
BSB renders καί as with to attach the seated figure.
BSB renders the repeated θρόνον ("throne") as it.
The participle καθήμενος ("one sitting") is used as a noun, rendered someone seated.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:3.sourceText: καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ὅμοιος ὁράσει λίθῳ ἰάσπιδι καὶ σαρδίῳ, καὶ ἶρις κυκλόθεν τοῦ θρόνου ὅμοιος ὁράσει σμαραγδίνῳ.
4:3.targetText: The One seated there looked like jasper and carnelian, and a rainbow that gleamed like an emerald encircled the throne.

groups.note: The article with the participle καθήμενος ("the one sitting") is rendered The One seated.
ὁράσει ("in appearance") is rendered looked.
The adverb κυκλόθεν ("around") is rendered as the verb encircled; the Greek has no verb.
ὁράσει ("in appearance") is rendered gleamed.
The adjective σμαραγδίνῳ ("emerald-like") is rendered as the noun an emerald.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.
BSB leaves λίθῳ ("stone") untranslated; jasper already names the stone.

English adds a relative; the Greek has none.

4:4.sourceText: καὶ κυκλόθεν τοῦ θρόνου θρόνους εἴκοσι τέσσαρας, καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς θρόνους εἴκοσι τέσσαρας πρεσβυτέρους καθημένους περιβεβλημένους ἐν ἱματίοις λευκοῖς, καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν στεφάνους χρυσοῦς.
4:4.targetText: Surrounding the throne were twenty-four other thrones, and on these thrones sat twenty-four elders dressed in white, with golden crowns on their heads.

groups.note: Same number, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The article τούς points back to the thrones just named; BSB renders it these.
The participle καθημένους ("sitting") is rendered sat.
BSB renders καί as with to attach the crowns.

4:5.sourceText: καὶ ἐκ τοῦ θρόνου ἐκπορεύονται ἀστραπαὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ βρονταί· καὶ ἑπτὰ λαμπάδες πυρὸς καιόμεναι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου, ἅ εἰσιν τὰ ἑπτὰ Πνεύματα τοῦ Θεοῦ·
4:5.targetText: From the throne came flashes of lightning, and rumblings, and peals of thunder. Before the throne burned seven torches of fire. These are the seven Spirits of God.

groups.note: φωναί ("sounds") is rendered rumblings.

The relative ἅ ("which") starts a new English sentence as These.

4:6.sourceText: καὶ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου ὡς θάλασσα ὑαλίνη ὁμοία κρυστάλλῳ· καὶ ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ κύκλῳ τοῦ θρόνου τέσσερα ζῷα γέμοντα ὀφθαλμῶν ἔμπροσθεν καὶ ὄπισθεν.
4:6.targetText: And before the throne was something like a sea of glass, as clear as crystal. In the center, around the throne, were four living creatures, covered with eyes in front and back.

ὁμοία ("like") is rendered by the comparison as … as.

4:7.sourceText: καὶ τὸ ζῷον τὸ πρῶτον ὅμοιον λέοντι, καὶ τὸ δεύτερον ζῷον ὅμοιον μόσχῳ, καὶ τὸ τρίτον ζῷον ἔχων τὸ πρόσωπον ὡς ἀνθρώπου, καὶ τὸ τέταρτον ζῷον ὅμοιον ἀετῷ πετομένῳ.
4:7.targetText: The first living creature was like a lion, the second like a calf, the third had a face like a man, and the fourth was like an eagle in flight.

groups.note: The participle ἔχων ("having") is rendered had.
The genitive ἀνθρώπου ("of a man", that is, a man's face) is rendered a man.
The participle πετομένῳ ("flying") is rendered in flight.

4:8.sourceText: καὶ τὰ τέσσερα ζῷα, ἓν καθ’ ἓν αὐτῶν ἔχων ἀνὰ πτέρυγας ἕξ, κυκλόθεν καὶ ἔσωθεν γέμουσιν ὀφθαλμῶν· καὶ ἀνάπαυσιν οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς λέγοντες Ἅγιος ἅγιος ἅγιος Κύριος ὁ Θεός ὁ Παντοκράτωρ, ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος.
4:8.targetText: And each of the four living creatures had six wings and was covered with eyes all around and within. Day and night they never stop saying:  “Holy, Holy, Holy, is the Lord God Almighty, who was and is and is to come!”

groups.note: Same number, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
ἓν καθ’ ἕν ("one by one") is rendered each.
The genitive αὐτῶν ("of them") is rendered by of before the four living creatures.
The participle ἔχων ("having") is rendered had.
γέμουσιν ("they are full of") is rendered was covered with, agreeing with each.
ἀνάπαυσιν … ἔχουσιν ("they have rest") is rendered they … stop.
The article belongs to Θεός; BSB places its the before Lord God.
The article with the finite verb ἦν works as a title ("the one who was"), rendered who was.
The article with the participle ὤν ("the one who is") is rendered is.
The article with the participle ἐρχόμενος ("the one coming") is rendered is to come.

4:9.sourceText: Καὶ ὅταν δώσουσιν τὰ ζῷα δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν καὶ εὐχαριστίαν τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ τῷ ζῶντι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων,
4:9.targetText: And whenever the living creatures give glory, honor, and thanks to the One seated on the throne who lives forever and ever,

groups.note: The future δώσουσιν ("will give") after ὅταν is rendered give.
The article with the participle καθημένῳ ("the one sitting") is rendered the One seated; the dative supplies to.
The article with the participle ζῶντι ("the one living") is rendered who lives.
The genitive τῶν αἰώνων ("of the ages") completes the idiom forever and ever; there is no separate Greek and.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB lists the first two gifts with a comma, so καί has no English word.

4:11.sourceText: Ἄξιος εἶ, ὁ Κύριος καὶ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, λαβεῖν τὴν δόξαν καὶ τὴν τιμὴν καὶ τὴν δύναμιν, ὅτι σὺ ἔκτισας τὰ πάντα, καὶ διὰ τὸ θέλημά σου ἦσαν καὶ ἐκτίσθησαν.
4:11.targetText: “Worthy are You, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honor and power, for You created all things; by Your will they exist and came to be.”
